# Restore the missing locked-file observations

The admitted native observation at source commit `3fc4cf7` failed: actual `3c41aa` returned outer exit 1, with controller exit 0, unchanged inputs and `receipt_valid=false`. The generated interrupted controller recorded five successful write opens after retirement. It omitted the five required sharing refusals while the files were protected. Preserve this result as failed; do not change its receipts or relabel it after a later run.

Repair only the generated driver in a fresh `_scratch/interrupted-owner-prelock-repair03`. Start from the frozen `generated_adapter_flow.py` in `_scratch/interrupted-owner-retirement-repair02`, SHA-256 `6a008136802d614ead53297f030dda3da01767ca8a63d313421f142c4d8a160b`. In `controller_interrupted_recovery_flow`, add the existing write-access refusal probe for each of the five expected files after the actual adapter has admitted its protected read set and acknowledged the worker policy, before issuing the generated media ticket or advancing the stream. Append the actual observations in order. A failed refusal must propagate through the existing context cleanup; never manufacture a row.

Keep the existing five post-retirement probes and all assertions unchanged. The launcher must still require ten observations: five error-32 refusals followed by five successful opens that write zero bytes. Do not reinterpret the old parent-guard field, claim final state for the terminated child, alter the fixed interruption or change worker/journal retirement. Preserve every old controller and the other core modules byte for byte. This corrects missing generated-driver evidence; the failed result alone does not establish a Windows sharing violation or production safety.

Deliver the full derivative, an exact mechanical diff, before/after hashes and a short review verdict. Add a separate inert regression that exercises this controller boundary: the five refusals precede ticket/transcription/segment work, the five successful probes follow retirement, and a refusal-check error prevents later work while reaching context cleanup. Keep the original 28 cases, 57 subtests and their fixtures/assertions unchanged. If the existing harness cannot exercise the boundary, document the concrete missing seam before expanding it. Do not add unrelated controls.

Prepare a fresh fake qualification with the original 28 cases plus only the new boundary cases. Root must review its complete source delta, loader/guard changes, expected cases and exact input map before one author run and one independent copy. Use the existing isolated Python host and protections. Retain actual results, including failures. Any failure needs its own diagnosis and repair; no automatic retry.

After those qualifications pass, prepare a fresh native proposal/run label ending in `02`. Its launcher predicates remain identical to run01; only the label, mapped source/hash bindings and admission references may change. Preserve the old proposal, false template and actual admission. Native source preparation grants no execution authority: root must review and admit the exact new invocation separately.

No model, checkpoint, D2 output, installed support file, physical journal or generated native fixture access is authorized by this source brief. Do not execute Python, native calls or the proposed controller during preparation. Keep the existing budgets and all live-index, port-5179, paid-API, new-fetch and D3/D4 restrictions. Production integration, the full candidate tree, packaging and installation remain later work; website and marketing stay paused.
